variants.headline: Party names a new leader
variants.sub: Leadership of {party} has changed, with {new} the new leader.
variants.body:
The party {party} has a new leader: {new}. A change at the head of an organisation is a political fact; a change in its programme is a separate question. Readers considering {target} should not have to accept the second as a necessary consequence of the first.

Management readers understand that a change in leadership is not a complete strategy document. Commercial judgment requires a disciplined distinction between the established development and assumptions about its practical consequences.

variants.headline: Leadership changes hands
variants.body:
Leadership of {party} has changed, with {new} the new leader. The event invites attention to what leadership means, beyond the identity of the person holding it. In assessing {target}, the useful question concerns responsibility for a political organisation rather than an invented personal history.

Management readers understand that a change in leadership is not a complete strategy document. Commercial judgment requires a disciplined distinction between the established development and assumptions about its practical consequences.

variants.headline: A new name at the head of the party
variants.sub: The party {party} has a new leader: {new}.
variants.body:
The new leader of {party} is {new}. That is the established development in {colony}. Any assessment of {target} should leave unreported policies, internal vote totals and explanations for the change outside the factual account of the event.

Management readers understand that a change in leadership is not a complete strategy document. Commercial judgment requires a disciplined distinction between the established development and assumptions about its practical consequences.
